translator.provenance: Receipt i18n/receipts/canvas-picker-1041-hi-translator.json: 1,041 initial translations on kimi-k3.1-pro; 20 values later revised on radient/auto; no automatic fallback reported.

scope: 8 hi namespace files at head 936e3a483b4d675c9827be5f40167da186f86900; every hi value added or changed by the batch (1,079: 1,041 manifest keys + 38 pre-existing keys backfilled in ui.chat.pickers (34) and ui.common.viewer (4)) read against the English source and its context sidecar. Full namespace key sets checked: 0 missing, 0 extra.
method: Read every scoped hi value with its English source and the English context sidecar (role/tone/note/placeholders/length) at the audited head.
Byte-compared en and hi; every exact match among the scoped values classified as IDENTICAL_OK with a technical/product reason, or as a stub. Stubs: 0.

Parsed every scoped value with @formatjs/icu-messageformat-parser; compared argument names, number/date skeletons, plural/select option sets, tag names and pound nodes; then rendered every plural/select message through intl-messageformat at hi counts 0, 1, 2 and 5 (260 renders, 0 errors).
Checked hi CLDR categories: one/other with 0 selecting one; every plural has one and other; no locale-inappropriate few/two/zero.
Checked NFC, manual bidi controls, Devanagari digits, danda/ASCII period usage, space-before-punctuation, register (आप only, कृपया only where English says please, no तुम/तू, no !).

Compared key sets per namespace (0 missing, 0 extra); read call sites for values whose meaning, gender or referent depended on composition (inline-edit status, session date range, emitted/excluded metric, pager range, image lightbox, find/replace switch, import naming).
Read the translator receipts but did not treat their summaries as evidence; the findings above were verified from catalogue bytes and code at the audited heads.

identical_summary.note: Counts only exact matches among the batch’s own values; each has a suggested IDENTICAL_OK reason in namespaces[*].identical_to_en.

observations: Shared namespaces with the surfaces batch: ui.common.actions, ui.common.speech, ui.common.updates and ui.common.viewer carry 6, 0, 127 and 4 common keys; 0 common keys differ in value, so a hand-union is semantically safe. The merged files will contain more keys than either head, so these four hashes will not bind the post-merge bytes; re-hash after the union before the ledger binds them.

The canvas translator receipt's per-namespace target hashes name an uncommitted worktree snapshot (worktree_head eb963e1baa63 has no committed hi files) and do not bind this head; this audit records the actual head hashes above. Its unresolved_issues also lists the 38 backfill keys as absent, but commit 5d094c59d8 restored them at this head, so they were audited here.

ui.chat.pickers.stop.confirm adds an exact `=0` arm not present in English: without it hi CLDR selects `one` for 0 and reads 'इस सत्र को रोकें' (stop this session) for zero. The branch is deliberate and renders correctly at 0/1/2; recorded as an observation, not a finding.

Key order in the newly created ui.chat.pickers and ui.common.viewer hi files does not follow the English key order, though the key sets are equal. Not a translation defect; flagging it for merge/union handling.

Quote style: batch prose keeps ASCII quotes (e.g. "{filename}.{filetype}") while the hi style guide prefers “ ”. The existing hi catalogue is mixed (64 ASCII double quotes vs 25 curly), so this is a locale-wide typography inconsistency, not counted as a per-key finding.
verdict: changes_requested — 0 blocker, 6 major, 9 minor, 2 nit across 8 namespace(s); 1,079 values read; 45 exact matches classified IDENTICAL_OK; 0 untranslated stubs.

findings.reason: This is the aria-label of the tab strip's role=tablist (canvas-tabs.tsx), a list of open document tabs; the imperative दस्तावेज़ खोलें names an action and misdescribes the control to screen-reader users. The fr/es catalogues both use the noun phrase (Documents ouverts / Documentos abiertos).
Rendered as {change} {index} {of} {total} in the review bar (inline-edit.tsx), so बदलें 1 / 3 reads as an imperative command; the key is the status noun, matching change_125665's बदलाव.

की is the Hindi genitive particle, not the technical English key; the label reads नाम (का/की) and hides that the field is the variable's key, so keep the machine-facing word key Latin as glossary §1 does for keys and identifiers.
